title: Product lead / Eng lead sync journal - Marisol
body:
Meeting: 1:1 prep + rapid follow-ups with Ajay (Eng Lead)
Date for sync: 2026-03-11 (planning to review status + blockers)
Participants (planned): Ajay Rao (eng lead), Marisol Chen (prod), Tess Morales (optional for rollout Qs)
Duration: 30m
Objectives: align on small-batch rollout plan for Console/Dedicated customers, unblock Private on-prem memory regression, decide next-steps for API routing fallback policy and canary windows. Quick wins to ship this sprint.

Agenda (tight):
- 0–3m: Quick status (hot tickets, customer escalations)
- 3–12m: Dedicated capacity canary plan (who runs, trigger conditions, rollback)
- 12–20m: Private on-prem memory regression (root cause, mitigation, proposed timeline)
- 20–27m: API routing + model-variant fallback (policy opt-in, costs)
- 27–30m: Action items, owners, dates, parking lot

Pre-reads (skim):
- API-1283: "Canary strategy for dedicated customers" (Jira) - short summary below
- PR #987: runtime change to KV-cache eviction (impact on on-prem memory) - needs review
- Confluence draft: console rollout checklist (contains audit/logging steps)

Quick summary notes to self (what I want Ajay to confirm):
- Canary SLO: 95th p95 latency target for dedicated pool must remain <= 120ms for token stream baseline. If p95 breaches by 20% for 10m, auto-fallback to hosted small model variant. Confirm triggers and where it's implemented (console routing layer vs runtime).
- Autoscale hysteresis: current config scales up quickly but scales down after 30m. For predictable costs we might want 10m cooldown for scale-down for dedicated pools; ask tradeoffs.
- Private on-prem: regression surfaced in customer lab (memory growth under long context workloads). Need concrete RCA: is this kernel change (PR #987) or a config mismatch? If it's PR, what's the timeline for revert/patch?
- Observability gaps: no token-level cost breakdown surfaced for dedicated canary nodes (console metrics team to add). Ask Ajay for ETA and whether he wants a joint ask to infra.

Spikes / Technical risks I want visible in the meeting:
- Model-variant fallbacks may increase token costs (quantized v float) — need to model cost delta and ensure product folks can set a budget cutoff.
- KV-cache eviction change could surface in long-running private sessions -> customers may see growth in memory, need hotfix path.
- Autoscaling configuration complexity across Dedicated vs Private: we should consider a simplified policy template (low-risk) for early enterprise customers.

"3 asks" (short asks I will make):
1) Decide whether the canary fallback should be implemented in the routing plane (console) or in-runtime. Prefer console-level for faster rollback—ask Ajay's opinion.
2) Commit to a patch plan for PR #987 or a temporary revert by EOD of next Tue if root cause points to runtime kernel.
3) Approve a small observability spike (2d) to add token-cost-by-node metric for dedicated canary pool so we can instrument cost impact during rollouts.

Parking lot (if extra time):
- Demo checklist for customer-facing Dedicated preview (security review steps, KMS integration doc owner)
- Private deployment e2e test matrix (runbook owner?)

Follow-up action items (capture during meeting) - draft assignments:
- Ajay: review PR #987 and provide a verdict (revert / patch) by 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC.
- Tess: prepare a one-pager for stakeholders showing cost delta between model variants (quantized vs float) by 2026-03-13.
- Marisol (me): open a short RFC for console vs runtime fallback tradeoffs and circulate to eng/console teams by 2026-03-12.
- Ajay + Observability eng: ETA for token-by-node metric (target 2026-03-18) -> confirm in 1:1 next week.

Notes to capture live (placeholders):
- Ajay: "I lean console-level because rollback is simpler and it centralizes policy" (capture exact phrasing).
- Ajay: "PR #987 looks suspicious but we need a reproducer in CI infra" -> action: Tess to try synthetic workload and add a failing job.

Risk register (short):
- High: On-prem memory regression causes customer downtime -> mitigation: temporary revert + emergency patch + communicated timeline.
- Medium: Canary fallback increases cost -> mitigation: short canary window, monitor token-by-node metric, automated budget stop.

Quick decision radar (my proposed binary decisions to get in this 1:1):
- Implement fallback at console routing layer? (Yes/No) -> prefer Yes, but need Ajay sign-off.
- Revert PR #987 if clear reproducer? (Yes/No) -> prefer Yes to buy time for thorough fix.
- Ship dedicated canary this sprint if observability added? (Yes/No) -> Yes if token metric available.

Personal notes / tone cues to self: be concise, push for commitment on timelines, avoid overloading Ajay with long-term wishlist. Keep meeting focused on unblock + two decisions max. End with "Do you need anything from product right now to move these 3 asks?"

Post-meeting (template for quick follow-up email I will send):
Subject: Quick notes + action items from sync (Marisol / Ajay)
Body: short bullets: 1) decisions made, 2) owners & dates, 3) blockers requiring exec escalation. Attach links to PR/Jira.

-- end of prep journal --
